messages:
eric: Quick follow-up after the RFC review — still getting gaps in cost attribution when enrichment rewrites spans and the billing_key gets dropped. Im proposing a tiny 'cost-stitcher' service to capture pre-enrich mappings and serve quick lookups for reconciliation. Thoughts?

lina: Could you sketch the failure mode again? A tiny example would help.

eric: Sure. Flow:
```
// arrival
envelope: { envelope_id: E42, billing_key: tenant-123 }
// enrichment rewrites spans/trace ids and emits without envelope_id
trace: { trace_id: T99, spans: [...], billing_key: null }
```
Downstream billing join uses envelope_id or envelope-hash, but it sometimes isn't present after merge/normalize. We need an alternate join path.

sam: How is this different from the current "late billing lookup" consumer?

eric: Late lookup assumes we still have a stable trace/envelope key to query. In some paths the key is lost; the stitcher would proactively record small (key -> billing_key) entries at pre-enrich time so reconciliation can match on other candidate identifiers (envelope-hash, tenant-hmac, short span-fingerprint).

priya: Main worry: cardinality and storage cost. We ingest millions of envelopes/sec at peak. Storing a mapping per envelope sounds heavy.

eric: Totally. Constraints/mitigations I'm thinking:
- default TTL = 24h, configurable per-customer (up to 7d)
- storage: in-memory K/V (redis cluster) with LRU and per-tenant caps
- compact keys: tenant_hmac (8 bytes) + envelope_hash (12 bytes) => 20 bytes key, value just billing_key id (4 bytes)
- optional sampling for low-value tenants to reduce writes

maria: Have we considered an append-only compacted topic + small lookup layer (rocksdb sidecar) instead of redis? Better for cost but higher read tail latency.

eric: Good call. Tradeoffs:
- redis: extremely low read latency (good for sync reconciliation with small timeout), higher infra cost and eviction risk
- compacted kafka + local rocksdb: cheaper long tail storage, but requires warm reads/loaders and more operational complexity
- hybrid: hot-tenant writes to redis, cold writes go to compacted topic for async backfill

lina: Security/compliance: we must not persist PII. Store only keyed HMACs encrypted by KMS. Also rotate keys. Include proof points for auditors.

eric: Agreed. Plan: store tenant_id as hmac(tenant_id, kms_key) and encrypt billing_key with envelope-level KMS where needed. Keys rotated with our standard schedule.

obs-bot: infra-bot: created ticket INF-7550 "stitcher: storage options evaluation (redis vs rocksdb vs hybrid)" assigned @maria, @priya

sam: Operational concerns: eviction storms could cause large backfill loads. Need metrics and circuit breakers. Suggested metrics: stitcher.mappings.count, stitcher.hits, stitcher.misses, stitcher.evictions, stitcher.redis_latency_p50/95, stitcher.backfill_queue_length.

priya: SLOs: Reconciliation should try stitcher lookup with a short budget (50ms). On miss/timeout mark event as needing backfill and push to async requeue. User path must never block. Also define acceptable backfill window (e.g., 6h for billing accuracy).

eric: Implementation sketch:
1) pre-enrich emits tiny record to topic `stitcher.snapshots` with {tenant_hmac, envelope_hash, billing_key_id}
2) stitcher consumers write to redis/rocksdb following config
3) billing service: on lookup miss, query stitcher with 50ms timeout; if miss, emit `billing.pending_stitch` event for async recheck/backfill

config snippet:
```
stitcher:
  input_topic: stitcher.snapshots
  storage: redis # options: redis|rocksdb|hybrid
  redis_prefix: "st"
  ttl_seconds: 86400
  lookup_timeout_ms: 50
  sample_rate: 1.0
```

lina: Who owns the service & infra? My vote: eng-platform owns code/alerts, eng-infra owns provisioned redis clusters/backups. Need runbook for KMS rotation and eviction alerts.

maria: I'll prototype the storage cost model for redis vs compacted topic this week and post numbers. Also will add an estimate for 99th percentile extra read QPS on billing path.

priya: +1 to prototype if we constrain TTL and enable sampling per-tenant. Make sure we have per-tenant caps to avoid noisy-neighbor costs.

eric: Thanks. Action items: eric will draft a short RFC addendum covering storage options, data model, metrics, and SLOs; maria + priya will produce cost + ops estimates; lina will coordinate with security for KMS/compliance language. I'll open infra-prototypes PR once draft is ready.

lina: Please include alert thresholds in the RFC (e.g., eviction_rate > 0.1% sustained, redis_p95 > 50ms).

eric: Will do. Closing for now, will post RFC link once ready.
